summary:
# NOTES: THE PARADISE MYSTERY (J. S. Fletcher, single book)

Source: Gutenberg #5308. Setting: cathedral city Wrychester, England, May–June, one year-ish span. Narrative in close third; many chapters POV Bryce/Mary.

## CH I "Only the Guardian"
- Opening: Close of Wrychester; 13th-c. cathedral, spire, rooks; half-ruinous gateway. Ransford house: old, oak panelled, half hidden in corner of Close; surgery at side, reached by stone passage.
- Breakfast, fine May morning. Dr. Mark Ransford: tall, clean-shaven, bright-eyed, dark hair with grey streak, looks ~40, well-dressed, prosperous medical man. Dick (Richard) Bewery: 17, senior schoolboy, Latin textbook, eats eggs/bacon, cricket. Mary Bewery: 19–20 ("just twenty"), brown hair w/ gold tints, grey-blue eyes, tennis/golf.
- Martin's bell: bequest by Wrychester citizen Martin; rung 3 min before 9 am daily from smaller bell-tower. Dick bolts out window.
- Ransford: Dick can beat him to any spot in ¼ the time; knows short cuts. Mary: Dick doesn't smoke "because of growth and cricket."
- Mary's complaint: Pemberton Bryce (Ransford's assistant) proposed 3 times, latest at Mrs. Folliot's garden-party. Ransford: will "settle with him"; "if a woman said No... a man took it as final."
- Mary: "Not send him away?" Ransford: "He'll get another in two minutes."
- Mary asks for full story of parents. Ransford: father "John Bewery," early friend, man of business, died young with mother; he became guardian. Money in Ransford's hands, due at 21 (Mary's at 21, Dick's at 21). "Not a great lot." Mary asks: "have we been dependent on you?" Ransford: "No," a lie he admits privately.
- Ransford in surgery groans: "madly in love with her myself... only the guardian."
- Bryce enters surgery by side door.

## CH II "Making an Enemy"
- Bryce walks "as if occupant were asleep"; soft step. ~28–30, handsome, son of medical man of repute; 2 yrs with Ransford. Ransford dislikes him ("deep, sly, cunning"; watchful; eyes fasten on people).
- Bryce files nails; philosophy: woman's first answer not final ("what a woman thinks Monday..."). "What's your conception of a man?" Ransford: "That!" Bryce: "pegging away."
- Ransford: "You're not going to get my ward."
- Bryce: "There's no mystery about me... you can't say that as regards your ward."
- Gossip quoted: "Wards of Dr. Ransford... can't be more than forty-five himself... one would think there ought to be a chaperon."
- Bryce: "I could be a very bad enemy." Refuses to promise to respect her wishes ("signs of a changed mind").
- Ransford writes cheque for 3 months' salary (agreement: 3 months' notice or payment). Bryce doesn't take it.
- Bryce sees Mary w/ Sackville Bonham (stepson of Mr. Folliot, tall lad) in garden, laughing.
- Ransford leaves by side door, crosses Close.

## CH III "St. Wrytha's Stair"
- Bryce pockets cheque, packs hand-bag.
- Elderly stranger at patient door: slight, grey, worn face, tired eyes, expensive city clothes, new silk hat, diamond pin, furtive. Asks for Ransford: "once knew some one of that name." Bryce says Ransford gone to Deanery (big house far corner); suggests going "through Paradise." Stranger: "Paradise?" Bryce: enclosure between south porch and transept, tombs, trees. Stranger: "It's immaterial... I'll see him."
- Bryce plans to go to another doctor in city; rooms in quiet lane (Friary Lane), far side of precinct.
- Mary at side entrance: "I have nothing to say to you... brought it on yourself." Bryce: "Summarily turned out... as if I had been stealing the spoons." "This is my first reward—for devotion."
- Paradise: outer court of old cloisters; ivy walls; yew, cypress, gravestones; gigantic elm; broken stone stair to high doorway in nave wall (St. Wrytha's Stair); pathway to SE Close corner; wicket-gate in corner.
- Bryce sees Ransford leave postern in west porch, face white, agitated.
- Varner (mason, master-mason's staff), white-faced, runs out: "Foot of St. Wrytha's Stair... Dead." Saw man "flung" through upper doorway; jackdaws had distracted him; saw a hand at doorway edge; man tottered on step, turned, screamed, crashed on flags. 5–6 min ago.
- Body crumpled at nave/transept angle. Bryce: neck broken; "died just as we came up." Organ voluntary = 10 o'clock morning service.
- Bryce searches body: breast pocket empty; no card, no papers; purse with banknotes, gold, silver; in a compartment a scrap of curiously folded (cocked-hat) paper; Bryce pockets it.
- Inspector Mitchington (sharp-eyed, dark, quick) + constables. Varner: gallery "clerestory gallery," tourists go up; 2–3 stairs in turrets. Mitchington sends constable with Varner.
- Bryce runs to fetch Ransford; finds him in surgery "picture of despair," beating one hand on other.

## CH IV "The Room at the Mitre"
- Bryce says "a stranger... slightly-built, elderly, grey-haired." Bryce decides not to mention stranger's surgery visit. Ransford's surprised look; says "I saw such a man entering the Cathedral, a while ago."
- Varner to Mitchington: "gentleman's hand... white shirt cuff and bit of black sleeve."
- Ransford shows relief when no papers on body.
- Constable: saw dead man last night at door of the Mitre talking with a "tallish man."
- The Mitre (Monday Market, quaint inn; bow window). Landlady Mrs. Partingley. Register: "Mr. John Braden, London" (short) and "Mr. Christopher Dellingham, London" (tall). Arrived previous evening by 6:40 London train. Braden asked about Duke of Saxonsteade being at home; hired trap for 2:30 to Saxonsteade.
- Dellingham: bearded, tall, broad-shouldered; met Braden in train; Braden "from Australia," said England's green landscape pleasant; Dellingham thinks he had recently come from dry country; "North-Country accent... Yorkshire or Lancashire."
- Braden's room: small leather suit-case; all items new; half-dozen collars from Aristide Pujol, 82 Rue des Capucines, Paris; foreign-look shirts. No name/initials on linen. Book: History of Barthorpe (old calf binding, steel frontispiece; bought from book-barrow in London for one-and-six; shown to Dellingham in train). Barthorpe = Midlands market town (Bryce notes).
- Police-station: crowd; Mr. Stephen Folliot (big, heavy-faced, wealthy, rare-rose grower, Close resident) says he saw the man in Cathedral "five minutes to ten" going up inside stair to clerestory gallery.
- Bryce goes home to Friary Lane; examines scrap of paper.

## CH V "The Scrap of Paper"
- Scrap: quarter-leaf yellowed stout notepaper, creases worn:
  "In Para. Wrycestr. juxt. tumb. / Ric. Jenk. ex cap. xxiii. xv."
  = in Paradise, Wrychester, near/next to tomb of Richard Jenkins; from (ex) head/cap; 23, 15 (inches).
- Bryce's 6 questions: (1) who is Braden (Mark Ransford's Mitre name—"John Braden")? (2) why visit Duke? (3) did Ransford know him? (4) did Ransford meet him in Cathedral? (5) did Ransford fling him? (6) was that Ransford's agitation?
- Background: Ransford came to Wrychester few years before, bachelor, not looking his age. Brought Mary (19, "just left school") and Dick (16, entered Dean's School). Annual 2-month holiday with them since Dick's 10th year: France, Switzerland, Ireland, Scotland, Norway. No relatives' letters; no memories of parents.
- Club (Wrychester Club). Sackville Bonham "loquacious and forward." Sackville: stepfather's theory—Braden followed to gallery, seized, flung. Archdale (architect, well-known firm, holds cathedral retaining fee): clerestory floor worn smooth, slopes steeply toward doorway; theory: slip, shot out; Varner saw an outflung arm.
- Bryce to clerestory turret door (south transept) — placard "Closed by order of the Dean and Chapter"; policeman: Dean ordered shut after crowds; Dean: "I won't have the Cathedral turned into a peepshow!" Vergers saw/heard nothing.
- Paradise wicket: also closed (policeman).
- Dick Bewery + Betty Campany (librarian's daughter) arrive; refused. Dick: "Do you think it really was murder?" Bryce: "I wasn't first... Varner called me."
- Library (old picturesque bldg, corner of Close): Ambrose Campany (cheery, middle-aged, shock-headed, blue spectacles, book-lover, librarian of Dean and Chapter, 45 years there; writing Cathedral history). Present: old Simpson Harker (sharp eyes, stout walking-stick, retired tradesman, neighbour of Bryce in Friary Lane). (Also named "Simpson Barker" once in text.) Campany: book clue — "I'm not a detective—but there's a clue!"; Barthorpe man.

## CH VI "By Misadventure"
- Campany's theory: Barthorpe man; make inquiry there. Bryce asks where burial registers are: third shelf from bottom, two volumes (Cathedral; Paradise & cloisters).
- Index: "Richard Jenkins, died March 8th, 1715: buried, in Paradise, March 10th."
- Chart dated 1850 of Paradise tombs: no Richard Jenkins. Bryce pretends interest in Spelbanks (SE corner).
- Inquest (next morning). Witnesses: Dellingham; Mrs. Partingley; Folliot; Varner; Bryce (w/ Ransford as medical); Mitchington (telegram to Barthorpe police; reply: nothing known of any John Braden).
- Duke of Saxonsteade: big, bluff; never heard name; "unusually good memory for faces"; can't guess reason ("antiquary... pictures... bookman").
- Alexander Chilstone, manager London & Colonies Bank, Threadneedle Street: Braden opened account day before death; introduced as just from Australia (Melbourne refs); paid £10,000 draft from Melbourne agents; drew nothing; no cheque-book taken; arrived Charing Cross that morning from Paris overnight; "speculated in landed property."
- Times personal ad, read aloud by Coroner: "If this meets the eye of old friend Marco, he will learn that Sticker wishes to see him again. Write J. Braden, c/o London & Colonies Bank, Threadneedle Street, London." Ransford seemed to start.
- Archdale and master-mason repeat slip theory; Varner recalled, insists on hand/cuff; jury disbelieves; verdict: death by misadventure. Ransford visibly relieved. Harker picks up Barthorpe book.

## CH VII "The Double Trail"
- Mary notes Ransford distress. Dick: Varner now says sun gleamed on cuff-links. Ransford: "confused images."
- 2 days later at breakfast: Ransford to attend Braden funeral (11 o'clock brougham); Dr. Nicholson covers urgent calls. Asks Mary to order wreath from Gardales' (florists), take to St. Wigbert's Churchyard. Sackville meets her at florist's, buys lilies, accompanies her. Sexton points out grave.
- Mrs. Folliot (masculine voice, ~6 ft, Roman nose; dominates Wrychester; Dean flees her). To Bryce: why would Ransford send flowers to stranger? Mrs. Deramore (next door to Ransford) saw man cross Close "in straight line from Dr. Ransford's garden."
- Bryce: ad = Braden "Sticker"; "Marco" = Ransford (Mark). No claimant for £10,000 after 48 hrs; Bryce thinks name assumed.
- Bryce to Free Library: gazetteer: Barthorpe, 2000 inhabitants, north Leicestershire; battle in Wars of the Roses; stocking trade.
- Train; two men in smoking compartment: "Braden Medworth," village a mile or two outside Barthorpe.
- Barthorpe: old hotel in marketplace under parish church; smoking-room. Harker enters.

## CH VIII "The Best Man"
- Harker: "I'd no idea I should meet you." Bryce lies: "left Dr. Ransford... country practice." Harker: friend in Barthorpe; leaving next morning 11 o'clock.
- Harker's real action: consults local superintendent (his friend), orders plainclothes shadow on Bryce ("young fellow at the Peacock"; Harker = detective).
- Bryce spends day searching Barthorpe records; no Braden family.
- Next day: Braden Medworth (small, river, trout). Bryce to vicarage (youngish vicar): lends printed parish register (1570–ten years ago, with index); pretext: writing book on English surnames.
- Index: "Bewery," p. 387. Entry: "June 19th, 1891. John Brake, bachelor, of the parish of St. Pancras, London, to Mary Bewery, spinster, of this parish, by the Vicar. Witnesses, Charles Claybourne, Selina Womersley, Mark Ransford."
- Charles Claybourne (shoemaker, sexton & parish clerk 32 yrs, big spectacles, shop by bridge): Mary Bewery was governess at vicarage ("nice, sweet young lady"). Brake = banker; he and Ransford fished there 3 yrs; Ransford = doctor (set Thomas Joynt's wife's leg). Once thought Mary would favour Ransford; Brake won; Ransford best man. Predecessor: Rev. Thomas Gilwaters, M.A., Oxford, left for another parish; now listed in Crockford at Bayswater (London).
- Bryce copies entry; pays half-crown. Shadow reports Bryce left Peacock by 5:30 express to London.

## CH IX "The House of His Friend"
- Next morning 11 am, Gilwaters' book-lined parlour, Bayswater (near Westbourne Grove); water-colour of Braden Medworth over mantel. Gilwaters: silver-haired, elderly.
- Bryce's false story: wants to marry Mary Bewery, ward of Ransford.
- Gilwaters: Mary governess at Braden Medworth; came aged 19; married 4 years later (1891) to John Brake; no friends/relatives; schooled in North. Brake & Ransford: London young men; Ransford few yrs younger (medical student or assistant). Brake a bank manager. Mary & Brake engaged; Gilwaters expected Ransford.
- Brake's trial: 5 yrs after marriage (~17 yrs ago). In prison cell Gilwaters saw Brake: sullen. Brake: "I'm not going to say one word more to any man living... I shall be dead to the world... for ten years... I'll let the world see what revenge means! Go away!" Brake said wife not to be found; refused where wife/children are.
- Mrs. Brake sold all furniture and vanished; two children (one infant boy). Ransford sold Streatham practice, vanished abroad, same period. Rumours: Brake's wife to Australia/Canada; money hidden abroad.
- Newspaper cutting (Gilwaters' scrapbook), headed "BANK MANAGER'S DEFALCATION": Central Criminal Court; John Brake, 33, formerly manager of Upper Tooting branch of London & Home Counties Bank Ltd; pleaded guilty to embezzling; counsel Mr. Walkinshaw, Q.C.: "Brake had been wounded in the house of his friend"; "a wronged and deceived man"; "morally innocent"; "foolish and serious error of judgment"; judge: 10 years' penal servitude.
- Gilwaters: Brake embezzled £2–3,000 short; cash inspector; Brake's explanation swept aside.
- Bryce: Ransford = false friend. Bryce asks Gilwaters' guess; Gilwaters: Brake's hatred; double disappearance. Bryce says he'll "let you know later." Bryce's cover: "not a man of that complexion."

## CH X "Diplomacy"
- Bryce's theory (return train): Ransford ran off with Mrs. Brake; Braden came to Wrychester, met Ransford in Cathedral, Ransford threw him through doorway. Advertisement = ruse to attract info about Ransford. Bryce resolves to marry Mary "by fair means or foul."
- Golf-Club route, Wrychester Common, lonely wicket-gate by spinney; Bryce waylays Mary. Mary: "Do you call this manly conduct, Dr. Bryce?"
- Bryce: Ransford "in danger"; rumour Ransford knows more; "two persons saw" Ransford leave west porch (one = Bryce, fake). Bryce admits Braden came to surgery door, asked for Ransford, "had once known a Dr. Ransford." Mrs. Deramore saw him leave; told Mrs. Folliot; Mary: "So—it is talked about!"
- Mary goes home thinking; passes Folliots' garden door; Folliot gives her roses ("no such rose in England"; 3 years grafting). Folliot: Mrs. Deramore's tattle; Sackville was present; "Some people would want to know why Ransford didn't tell that." Mary: "supposing this man had been to our house?" Folliot: "When there's a bit of mystery..."

## CH XI "The Back Room"
- Lunch at 1:15 daily (cold, self-serve). Dick (from school): rumour Ransford "knows something." Ransford: "Daren't is a much more likely word than won't." Dick: Mrs. Deramore; son Jim Deramore. Ransford: "Dr. Ransford never saw any man, Braden or anybody else... that morning."
- Mary admits Bryce told her (in confidence); Ransford: "I dislike it... putting ourselves in his power." Go to Bryce's rooms: old house in Friary Lane, back of Close; double sitting-room, front window on one garden, back on another; curtains screen back room.
- Bryce: "Here's one of the police... Step inside there... Don't stick at trifles!" Ransford & Mary hide behind curtains.
- Mitchington (whisky-and-soda): rumour via "old dowagers." Bryce: Braden came to surgery, "merely to be told where the Cathedral Library was." (Mary knows Bryce lies.)
- Mitchington: Varner keeps talking. Collishaw (townsman, mason's labourer in Cathedral): drunk hints at a tavern "could tell something"; "squared"; Mitchington warned him of accessory charge. Mitchington's discovery: Braden out from before 9 pm until after 11 pm on first evening (left Mitre); "Where did he go?" Mitchington: "Keep it to yourself, doctor."
- Ransford: "You put that man off... You didn't tell him the truth." Bryce: Braden asked "if Dr. Ransford was in... once known a Dr. Ransford." Ransford: "We three... know this—I never saw Braden when he came to my house."

## CH XII "Murder of the Mason's Labourer"
- Bryce often in Library; Campany's drawings; shield with 3 crows/ravens; "Richard Jenkins, armiger." Campany: tomb in corner of Paradise near east wall of south porch bears arms; inscription gone; Richard Jenkins Welsh, settled 17th-c., left money to St. Hedwige's Church outside walls. Also Gervase Tyrrwhit tomb.
- After noon, Bryce into Paradise to see Jenkins tomb: finds Collishaw asleep (dead) at foot of nave wall, sunlight; clay pipe fallen; dinner on handkerchief (bread, cheese, onions); tin bottle with cork on string; shovel, wheelbarrow. Hands warm, rigid; died in sleep.
- Bryce sends Dick Bewery (going home to lunch) for Mitchington, "quietly."
- Bryce tastes bottle: cold tea, too much sugar.
- Mitchington: "Good Lord! It's Collishaw!" Dr. Ransford not at home: gone to Highminster (County Council), back at four (Dick). Dr. Coates (elderly, leading practitioner) fetched.
- Bryce: bottle and dinner remains to be locked up.
- Mitchington reveals: Ransford fetched to Collishaw's cottage 6 am (Mrs. Collishaw ill; Ransford attends her). Next-door Mrs. Batts' account: Ransford alone with Collishaw's tin bottle when Mrs. Batts fetched something.
- 5 pm: Coates: poisoned, "Hydrocyanic acid!" (H.C.N.)

## CH XIII "Bryce Is Asked a Question"
- Private room: Mitchington: "Poisoned... prussic acid." Not in tin bottle (Bryce: "I poured a few drops... cold tea... no H.C.N.... no bitter almonds").
- Bryce: "big bungler—or damned clever"; one drop instantaneous.
- Mitchington's locked drawer: small cardboard pill-box; label "One after meals.—Mr. Collishaw" in Ransford's handwriting; found in Collishaw's waistcoat pocket; 4 sugar-coated pills (box holds 6). Bryce: "Mere digestive pills."
- Bryce, en route to Ransford's house, meets Ransford and Mary returning from station. Ransford: "Miss Bewery has just told me." Bryce: "Collishaw was poisoned... H.C.N." Mentions Mitchington's suspicion, pill-box. Ransford: "Bah!" Bryce: "reveal it, and be done with the whole thing." Ransford refuses: "neither to be coerced, bullied, or cajoled."
- Ransford to Mary: "I don't trust that fellow Bryce... bad enemy." Mary asks again about her & Dick's past; Ransford: "I'm waiting for something—some particulars... in two days."
- Harker (archway of Paradise) invites Bryce to his tiny house behind Close: legal/criminal books, pictures, cabinet, whisky, cigars. Harker: "What have you done with that scrap of paper that you took out of Braden's purse?"

## CH XIV "From the Past"
- Bryce: "Who are you, Mr. Harker?" Harker: detective "five-and-twenty years" (Yard). Bryce: "retired policeman—detective branch."
- Harker: knew Braden; Braden came to Harker's house, same chair, "from five minutes past nine to close on ten o'clock the night before his death." (NB conflicts with Mitchington's "out ~9–11.")
- Harker's account: Harker arrested Brake at bank years ago; Brake wanted Harker's help with wife/children (answer: "looked after"). Met Brake in Market Place under standard lamp: "You're the very man I wanted to find!" Brake: left England; Canada, US, NZ, Australia; wool speculation; repaid bank every penny with interest 4 yrs ago (receipt); "My name ever since I left England... Braden—John Braden."
- Brake's commission: find "Falkiner Wraye" of Barthorpe (small estate agent, left ~17–18 years ago); said Barthorpe had "unpleasant memories"; written memo; £25 on account; Brake had paper: "Can you read Latin?" "it's a secret."
- Harker at Crown and Cushion tavern (after accident): saw Glassdale (fellow convict, forgery, same prison, release same time; Harker "never forgets a face"); Glassdale fled by train to junction.
- Harker went to Barthorpe: learned Wraye had been Barthorpe man, left 18 yrs ago; nothing more.
- Bryce confesses his Barthorpe searches. Harker: Brake's "Falkiner Wraye" was a fiction; "when we've found out what it does mean, we shall know a lot more."

## CH XV "The Double Offer"
- Harker: why did Brake want the Duke? Glassdale = Duke's former London estate agent; forged Duke's name on a cheque. Glassdale & Brake to tell Duke about stolen jewels. Harker: "95,000 offered" (sic; later Sackville says £5,000 standing reward).
- Harker's instructions: Bryce to search behind Jenkins tomb tomorrow night, alone, after dark; report to Harker. "We mustn't meet and talk in public."
- Collishaw inquest (next morning): foreman: Collishaw clearing rubbish at foot of south nave wall; dinner basket & tin bottle on box-tomb under a yew. Bryce's bare account. Doctors: hydrocyanic acid, taken few minutes before discovery.
- Ransford in box, angry; asked Coroner to ask Dr. Coates whether a digestive pill found in stomach; explains pills would delay death. Superintendent whispers; Coroner adjourns a week. Ransford: "I protest... I know nothing whatever of the causes of the deaths of either Collishaw or of Braden—upon my solemn oath!" Adjourned "to this day week."
- Sackville to Bryce on street (with Mr. Folliot nearby talking to Coroner): "Ransford is a perfect ass"; Folliot "going to take a hand"; Sackville claims understanding with Miss Bewery ("family interest"; "Caesar's wife").
- Night: Mitchington with two fresh handbills: £500 reward (signed Phipps & Maynard—Ransford's solicitors) for info on deaths of Braden & Collishaw; £1,000 reward (Beachcroft—Folliot's solicitor) for circumstances of Braden's death. Bryce's guess: Folliot wants son to marry Mary.
- Bryce slips out for Paradise.

## CH XVI "Beforehand"
- Bryce's kit: short tempered-steel crowbar, bull's-eye lantern (from iron-monger). Pavement of small squares, some with initials/dates; he'd need to lift 1–3 squares.
- Dick Bewery and Betty Campany's secret love-letters: cavity in old monument just inside Paradise wicket-gate ("love's post-office").
- Dick runs into Bryce on Friary Lane path: "There's something up in there—a search." Ring of metal on stone. Dick leads Bryce quietly through bushes. Five men by lamps: master-mason (kneeling, crowbar), Mitchington, a clergyman (lesser Chapter dignitary), Duke of Saxonsteade, and a tall stranger (Glassdale). They are probing square-by-square, not knowing exact spot.
- Bryce sends for Harker. Harker gives felt overshoes ("walk round your mother's bedroom"). Harker whispers: "Glassdale!"
- Master-mason: "Something here!" Lifts small coarse-sacking parcel, black sealing-wax blotches. Passed to Mitchington, then to Duke (delighted). "Let us go to your office, inspector."
- Dick slips off; Harker: "Whatever it is, the whole town'll know by tomorrow."
- Harker's scrap-book (cuttings, indexed): famous robbery at Saxonsteade ~15 years ago: Duchess's diamonds, stolen after grand ball; never traced. Harker: Glassdale told Duke; Brake and Glassdale intended to tell Duke together for reward. Harker's final question: "How did Brake come to his end?"

## CH XVII "To Be Shadowed"
- Dick tells Mary & Ransford story (rich detail). Ransford: "Master Bryce is playing a game!" Ransford: has "a little more patience"; will tell later. Rumours: "I'll let certain folk in Wrychester know what I think of them."
- ~10 pm: parlourmaid: Inspector Mitchington wants a word; with him Detective-Sergeant Jettison of the Yard (quiet, ordinary, "might have been half a dozen things").
- Mitchington's account: Duke's diamonds found in Paradise tonight; buried by thief; secret from Glassdale (informant; thief dead in Australia). Braden = John Brake, ex-bank manager, 10 yrs for embezzlement. Jettison's theory: Brake followed into gallery, robbed of diagram/paper, flung; Collishaw silenced.
- Mitchington asks Ransford for antecedents. Ransford sets terms: secrecy/word of police. Ransford reveals: Braden was at Harker's the evening of arrival; Ransford attending patient in house opposite Harker's; saw Harker take man in; man left ~1 hr later. Also: Harker & Bryce watched police operation.
- Ransford: "Bryce it was who discovered Collishaw... Bryce evidently had a motive in fetching Harker." Ransford: Campany remarked Bryce's archaeology interest.
- Jettison: "keep an eye on those two." Mitchington: will shadow both. Ransford: "in two days from now, I can tell you more."

## CH XVIII "Surprise"
- Walk home: Jettison: Ransford "knows more than he's telling." Jettison: Bryce medical, could poison Collishaw; theory of collusion Bryce–Harker. Mitchington: Harker "retired tradesman from London... potters about"; Bryce "reserved; keen on Ransford's ward."
- Mitchington & Jettison call on Bryce ~11:10 pm (he rarely sleeps before 1 am; reads statecraft, takes notes). Bryce's inner plan: bottle Ransford up via suspicion; save him, then demand Mary as price.
- Visitors tell Bryce about jewels. Bryce coolly: "I saw you busy... young Bewery told me... I fetched old Harker." Bryce: Harker = retired Yard man "Harker Simpson" (transposed name); "ask them at the Yard."

## CH XIX "The Subtlety of the Devil"
- Bryce, now sharp and resolute, declares he wants to marry Mary Bewery and knows more than anyone.
- Bryce's account: morning events (surgery visit; Ransford seen in west porch; Varner; Collishaw's death). Bryce's summary: Bewery children = Brake's children; marriage at Braden Medworth (entry seen); Brake's bank trouble; Harker arrested him; wife/children vanished.
- Bryce's theory: Ransford ran off with Brake's wife; Braden met Ransford in gallery; altercation; flung.
- Collishaw: widow found Friendly Society deposit book; £50 paid 2 days before death. Bryce's theory: hush-money paid by someone.
- Pill theory: poisoned pill (thick coating); "six pills in box, five left"; Ransford's post-mortem challenge = "bluff."
- Bryce: "Collishaw—murder, without doubt—deliberate." Accident for Braden possible; Varner's hand "might have been stretched out to pull Braden back."
- Bryce: Harker sent to London last train tonight, to check Ransford's whereabouts (lie). Napoleon quote: "The art of the police is not to see that which it is useless for it to see."
- Walk home: Jettison: "if that young doctor's playing a game... damned deep 'un... watch the lot."

## CH XX "Jettison Takes a Hand"
- Next morning: Ransford went to London by 8:15 train (telegram). Bryce left on bicycle 8:30, landlady says "into the country."
- Jettison writes letters; visits Wrychester Second Friendly Society, Fladgate; secretary George Stebbing (sandy, freckled, "Wrychester Second Friendly Society—George Stebbing, Secretary"). Collishaw paid £50 "in gold" (fifty sovereigns in a bag), 2 days before death; member 14 years; savings £2–3 per half-year.
- Banks: Old Bank (Monday Market); Popham & Hargreaves (Square); Wrychester Bank (Spurriergate).
- Jettison's discovery (3rd bank): day before Collishaw's payment, Bryce drew £50 in gold (cheque to self). Jettison: Bryce would not pay hush-money because Bryce not in accident.
- Foreman's abstract (Mitchington's notes): Collishaw in north gallery clearing timber 9 to past 11; uninterrupted view of gallery & arched doorway at head of St. Wrytha's Stair.
- Jettison: "somebody else" in it (Harker's claimed Yard status unverified; Mitchington never heard of it).
- Bryce not at rooms (landlady: out since early morning; dinner ordered 7).
- Telegram: "Meet me with Jettison Wrychester Station on arrival of five-twenty express from London mystery cleared up guilty men known—Ransford." Jettison: "he says men, not man!"

## CH XXI "The Saxonsteade Arms"
- Bryce rides ~10 miles to Saxonsteade (woods, valleys); goal: find Glassdale.
- Saxonsteade Arms (old coaching inn, ducal arms on sign). Glassdale in garden, going as "Mr. Gordon." Bryce gives card; claims he knows Duke.
- Glassdale: knew Braden for years; "Never knew he had a daughter"; never heard of Ransford or Braden's wedding; Brake's motive: Duke's jewel secret (entrusted by dying man in Australia) and revenge on Falkiner Wraye (+ partner Flood): Wraye & Flood tricked Brake into lending bank's money "for a couple of days," then vanished.
- Wraye description (Brake's): big man, clean-shaven, bad scar on LEFT jaw, lost MIDDLE finger of LEFT hand (gun accident). Bryce drops pipe; recognizes. "Left hand—left jaw! Unmistakable!"
- Glassdale suggests the police never checked "Dellingham" (who vanished). Bryce gives handbills to Glassdale. Glassdale resolves to go to Wrychester at once.

## CH XXII "Other People's Notions"
- Bryce decides to see Mary; lunches with Sackville at golf club. Sackville: "wheels within wheels"; £5,000 reward; "we must clear" Ransford; Folliot's reward; Sackville "doing a bit underground."
- Mary at home: Mr. Folliot visits (roses); asks whether anyone applied for Ransford's reward; Mary refuses comment; Folliot evasive.
- Mrs. Folliot visits: claims she insisted husband offer £1,000 reward; expects union with Sackville. Mary: "I've no more intention of marrying Mr. Sackville Bonham than of eloping with the Bishop!" Mrs. Folliot leaves.
- Bryce approaches; sees Mrs. Folliot leaving.

## CH XXIII "The Unexpected"
- Mary receives Bryce in garden summer-house (beech trees). Bryce: Ransford "in serious and imminent danger... arrest... tonight."
- Bryce describes police theory: motive (Ransford ran off with Braden's wife); Braden flung; Collishaw silenced. Mary: "No man of any real sense would believe it."
- Mary sees through him: "you came here to bargain with me... you were to save Dr. Ransford, and for reward you were to have me." Calls him "bad, wicked, base." "Mind the wheel doesn't come full circle... go away and don't dare to come near me again."
- Bryce sees Folliot emerge from garden door with Glassdale. Bryce leaves hurriedly.

## CH XXIV "Finesse"
- Glassdale in Wrychester: reads two handbills; goes to solicitor for £1,000 offer (Beachcroft). Solicitor: principal "Mr. Stephen Folliot, The Close"; instructs info to principal only.
- Glassdale at Folliot's garden (roses): "I think he met at least one of 'em here... perhaps both." Folliot: "a very particular friend" of his who incurred Braden's hatred. Names given: Falkiner Wraye; Flood. "Revenge!" Folliot: "come and see me this evening... just about dusk to that door."
- Folliot sees Bryce coming over Close; beckons.

## CH XXV "The Old Well House"
- Folliot leads Bryce to old grey-stone well-house in far corner of garden (ivy, high trees; 100-ft dry well; trap-door w/ iron ring; upstairs snuggery, luxurious).
- Bryce: Glassdale's visit; "I know a good deal"; tells Brake/Wraye history; claims Folliot = Falkiner Wraye; shows finger & jaw. Bryce asks whose hand Varner saw; Folliot: "Not mine"; "the other man" (Flood); refuses to name; "Nothing can prove... that I ever met Braden." Folliot says never knew Brake married/had children; "never heard Brake speak of any Ransford."
- Bryce: "Those two wards of Ransford's are Brake's girl and boy!" Folliot: "Who's Ransford, then?"
- Folliot sees Mitchington, Jettison, Glassdale (led by gardener) through pergola. Folliot pulls revolver: fires at Glassdale; bullet hits Bryce through heart; Bryce dies. Folliot takes poison, sits, dies.

## CH XXVI "The Other Man"
- ~5 pm: Glassdale at police-station: "Folliot... that's Wraye." Mitchington incredulous. Glassdale: Folliot "admitted it... as good as done so." Glassdale says "there's another man" (Flood). Glassdale's "hush-money" ploy.
- Ransford arrives by train, with Harker (who travelled with him from London). Ransford: bank in London (where Braden lodged money) investigation; agents traced Flood; Flood = Fladgate, verger (Folliot got him appointed). Wraye = Folliot.
- Mitchington & party to Fladgate's cottage (fifth cottage down narrow lane off High Street, near Close; alone). Fladgate, tall, clean-shaven, solemn: "Your real name is Flood!"
- Flood's confession: he was Wraye's agent in London money-dealings; Brake recognized him in gallery that morning; Brake seized his arm, struggled, cried out; organ playing loudly; Brake slipped at open doorway; "sheer, pure accident." Flood told Wraye, who forced silence. Wraye told Flood he'd paid Collishaw £50; Flood heard of Collishaw's sudden death, believes Wraye.
- Mitchington sends constables to guard Flood; moves to Folliot's (via back way). Mrs. Folliot out; Sackville at golf links.
- Folliot in well-house: sees Harker & Ransford following; asks Bryce "You've no hand in this?" Bryce: "I never knew till just now!" Folliot: "Go down! Let 'em in... I'll settle with 'em." Bryce realizes his schemes are ruined. Bryce tells Mitchington "He's upstairs!" Mitchington brushes him aside.
- Upstairs: Folliot fires at Glassdale; Glassdale dodges; bullet kills Bryce. Folliot poisons himself (same poison as Collishaw), dies in chair.

## CH XXVII "The Guarded Secret"
- Mary had planned to tell Ransford all Bryce said; waited at dining-room window; 6 pm Ransford across Close with Dick, turns into Folliot's garden.
- Dick tells Mary: "Folliot and Bryce are both dead!"; Folliot shot Bryce, then poisoned himself "the same stuff that finished that chap Collishaw." Fladgate (verger) real name Flood; police have him.
- Ransford enters; relief visible; "I've wanted to tell both of you... until today... I didn't know everything."
- Ransford's account: John Brake = "John Braden" = their father. Brake friend of Ransford in London young men; met Mary Bewery in Leicestershire; Ransford best man. Falkiner Wraye & Stephen Folliot = same person; Flood = Fladgate. Wraye & Flood persuaded Brake to lend bank's money for short deals; decamped with it; bank found shortfall; Brake prosecuted, no defence.
- Before arrest Brake sent for Ransford; had Ransford take wife & children to a quiet country place; wife assumed maiden name; wife died within a year (not strong). Brake, after conviction, wanted Wraye & Flood found before he'd see children. Ransford searched years; no trace. Brake released; went abroad (clue: Wraye in America) to hunt them.
- Ransford: saw Brake on morning of death going up galleries (west porch / south aisle); Brake didn't see him; Ransford came home agitated; Bryce saw him.
- Ransford: Braden's death accident (believes Fladgate's account); Folliot poisoned Collishaw ("Folliot knew that if the least thing came out about Fladgate, everything would come out about himself").
- Dick: "Well, Folliot's done for!... I wanted to know for certain about the other."
- Ransford & Mary alone: Mary: "Why didn't you tell me?" Ransford: wanted father's memory cleared first. Mary: "Hadn't you seen that I wanted to share all your trouble?" Ransford: "you don't mean that you can care for an old fellow like me?" Mary smiles, comes closer: "You must have been very blind not to have seen that for a long time!" (END)
